title: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: This test measures the level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which is made by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain. FSH plays a role in sexual development in children and in fertility in adults.
context: What a result means depends on your sex and age. In people who menstruate, FSH changes through the monthly cycle, so testing may be done at a set time; from about age 45, higher FSH is often a normal sign of perimenopause and menopause.
aboveRange: A higher level is often associated with the ovaries or testicles not making usual levels of sex hormones, so the pituitary makes more FSH
In people who menstruate this can be linked to menopause, PCOS, or primary ovarian insufficiency; in men it can be linked to a condition affecting the testicles
belowRange: A lower level is often associated with a condition of the pituitary gland or hypothalamus
In people who menstruate, a lower level may also be linked to rapid weight loss, being very underweight, or extreme exercise
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
